label: first paragraph
text: The purpose of this Act is the comprehensive protection of personal data included in files, records, databases or other data processing technical means -whether public or private- used for reporting purposes, in order to guarantee the right of individuals to their honor and privacy, as well as access to information recorded thereupon, in accordance with the third paragraph of Article 43 of the National Constitution.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: second paragraph
text: The provisions of this Act shall also apply, if appropriate, to such data related to legal persons.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: third paragraph
text: Under no circumstances shall databases or media information sources be affected hereby.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: introductory
text: The following terms shall have the following meanings to the effects of this Act:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: first paragraph
text: Data file creation shall be lawful provided that it is duly registered in compliance with the principles set forth herein and rules and regulations passed as a consequence thereof.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: second paragraph
text: Data files shall not have any purpose contrary to laws or public morals.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Personal data collected for processing thereof shall be true, appropriate, relevant, and not excessive in relation to the scope and purpose for which they have been obtained.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Data collection shall not be carried out by anti-trust or fraudulent means, or by means contrary to the provisions of this Act.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. Data subject to processing shall not be used for purposes other than, or incompatible with, those purposes that led to their collection.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 4. Data shall be accurate and updated if necessary.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 5. If any data is known to be inaccurate or incomplete, such totally or partially inaccurate data or incomplete data shall be deleted and replaced or, if applicable, supplemented, by the person in charge of the file or database, notwithstanding holder’s rights set forth in Article 16 hereof.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 6. Data shall be stored in such a way that they allow the holder thereof to exercise the right of access thereto.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 7. Data shall be destroyed whenever it is no longer necessary or relevant for the purposes for which it has been gathered.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Processing of personal data shall be unlawful if the holder has not given free, express and informed consent thereupon, in writing or evidenced by any other similar means, according to the relevant circumstances.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: 1 second paragraph
text: The above referred consent, given with other representations, shall be expressly stated and highlighted, with the prior notice to the person from which data is required, which notice shall include information described in Article 6 hereof.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Consent shall not be necessary if:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: introductory
text: When gathering personal data, holders thereof shall be previously notified, expressly and clearly, about the following:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. No person shall be bound to provide private data.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Private data shall only be gathered and subject to processing provided that there are reasons of general public interest authorized by law. Private data may also be processed for statistical or scientific purposes when holders thereof cannot be identified.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. The creation of files, databases or records storing information which directly or indirectly discloses private data is hereby forbidden. Notwithstanding, the Catholic Church, religious associations, and political organizations and unions may maintain records of their members.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 4. Data related to criminal or misdemeanor records may only be subject to processing by competent public authorities, within the framework of the respective acts and rules and regulations.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: Public or private health care centers and practitioners working on health science-related fields may gather and handle personal data related to the physical or mental health of patients attending such centers, or who are or have been under treatment, respecting the professional secret principle.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. The person in charge of the data file or the user thereof shall adopt all technical and organizational measures necessary to ensure the security and confidentiality of personal data, so as to prevent such data from being forged, lost, inquired, or processed without authorization, and allowing to detect any information deviation, whether intentional or not, whether risks arise from a human act or from the technical means in use.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. It is hereby forbidden to record personal data in files, registers, or databases not compliant with technical integrity and security conditions.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. The person in charge and those involved in any phase of personal data processing shall be bound to keep the professional secret with respect thereto. Such obligation shall outlive the relationship with the data file holder.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. The person bound to keep the professional secret may be released from such obligation by court decision, and provided that there are reasons of public security, national defense or public health.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Personal data subject to processing may only be assigned to comply with purposes directly related to the lawful interest of both assignor and assignee, with prior consent of the data owner, who shall be informed about the purpose of the assignment. Identity of the assignor and elements allowing such assignor to assign such data shall be specified.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Assignment consent shall be revocable.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. Consent shall not be necessary in the following cases:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 4. The assignee shall be subject to the same legal and regulatory obligations of the assignor, and the assignor shall be jointly and severely liable for compliance thereof to the competent authority and the relevant data owner.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Transfer of personal data of any kind to any country or international or supranational organization is hereby forbidden if adequate protection is not provided.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. This shall not apply in the following events:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: Any person may request information from the appropriate authority in relation to personal data files, records, or databases, the purposes thereof and the identity of the persons in charge. The record maintained to such effect shall be available to public inquiry free of charge.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. The data owner, with the prior identity proof, shall be entitled to request and obtain information about his/her personal data included in public or private databases intended for reporting purposes.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. The person in charge or the user of such databases shall provide the requested information within ten calendar days as of notice thereupon. If such ten-day period has elapsed and the request has not been met, or if the report furnished is insufficient, an action for protection of personal data or habeas data action may be commenced as provided for in this Act.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. The right of access referred to in this Article may only be exercised free of charge once every six months, save a lawful interest is evidenced to such effect.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 4. Exercise of the right referred to in this Article in the case of personal data or deceased individuals shall correspond to general heirs.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Information shall be provided in a clear way, free from any coding and, if applicable, accompanied by an explanation of terms used, in a language understood by the general public.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Information shall be comprehensive and related to the entire holder's record, even when the requirement is only related to one aspect of personal data. In no event shall the report disclose any third-party data, even though they may be related to the interested party.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. Information, at the holder’s option, may be furnished in writing, by electronic means, telephone, images, or by any other means competent to such end.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Any person shall be entitled to have his/her personal data, included in a database, edited, updated and, if applicable, deleted or subjected to confidentiality rules,.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. The person in charge or the user of such database shall proceed to edit, delete or update personal data of the party involved, carrying out the necessary actions to such end within a maximum of five business days following receipt of the data owner’s claim, or information on the error or untruthfulness.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. Non-compliance with this obligation within the term agreed upon in the above subArticle, shall authorize the party involved to file an action for protection of personal data or habeas data action provided for herein.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 4. In the case of assignment or transfer of data, the person in charge or the user of the database shall serve notice of the change or deletion upon the assignee within five business days following the data editing or deletion.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 6. Deletion shall not proceed in the event that it may damage third party lawful rights or interests, of if there is a legal obligation to preserve the integrity of such data.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 7. During the relevant process of data verification and rectifying of the error or untruthfulness, the person in charge or the user of the database shall block the file, or state --at the time of providing information related thereto-- the fact that that such information is subject to revision.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 8. Personal data shall be kept intact during the terms provided for in the applicable provisions or, if applicable, in contractual provisions agreed upon between the person in charge or the user of the database and the data owner.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Persons in charge or users of public databases may, for reason, deny access, editing or deletion of data to protect the Nation's defense, public order and security, or to protect third party rights or interests.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Information about personal data may also be denied by persons in charge, or users, of public databases if it hinders pending judicial or administrative actions related to the investigation of compliance with tax or pension duties, the discharge of health and environmental oversight functions, investigation of crimes and identification of administrative violations. The resolution in force to establish such denial must state the reasons thereof, and notice thereupon shall be served on the party involved.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. Notwithstanding the provisions of the above subArticles, if the party involved has to exercise the right of defense in a legal proceeding, access to records shall not be forbidden.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: The National Defense Committee and the National Congress Bicameral Committee on Oversight of Domestic Security and Intelligence Agencies and Activities, and the House Domestic Security Committee, or any committees that may replace them, shall have access to files or databases referred to in Article 23, subArticle 2, for reason, and with regard to those aspects constituting the subject matter of such Committees competence.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: Editing, updating or deletion of inaccurate or incomplete personal data included in public or private records shall be carried out free of charge.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Court decisions or administrative acts implying an assessment of human conduct shall not be based solely on the results of computer processed personal data that may give a definition of the involved party profile or personality.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Any acts contrary to the precedent provision shall be null and void.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Any public or private file, record, or database intended for reporting purposes shall be recorded with the Registry authorized by the competent authority to such effect.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Registration of databases shall comprise, at least, the following information:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. No data user may have personal data of any nature different from the nature of data stated in the record.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: closing paragraph
text: Non-compliance with these requirements shall imply administrative sanctions provided for in chapter VI hereof.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Rules governing the creation, editing or deletion of files, records or databases belonging to public agencies shall be passed by general provisions published in the National Official Gazette or in an authorized newspaper.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. The respective provisions shall state the following:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. The provisions passed for deletion of computer records, the destination thereof or such measures taken to destroy them shall be expressly stated.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Personal data that, having been stored for administrative purposes, must be included as permanent record in databases belonging to the armed forces, security forces, police departments or intelligence agencies shall be subject to the provisions hereof; as well as data relating to personal records furnished by such databases to administrative or court authorities that may require them by virtue of standing legal provisions.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Processing of personal data for the purposes of national defense or public security by the armed forces, security forces, police departments or intelligence agencies, without the consent of the parties involved, shall be limited to those events and data categories necessary for strict compliance with the missions legally assigned to them for national defense or public security purposes, or to fight against crime. In such cases, files shall be specified and identified to such effect, and they shall be classified in categories, according to their degree of reliability.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. Personal data registered for police purposes shall be deleted whenever they become no longer necessary for the investigation that gave rise to their storage.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: Private persons creating files, records, or databases not intended exclusively for personal use shall register as provided for in Article 21.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Whenever personal data processing services are delivered on behalf of third parties, such data shall not be applied or used for a purpose other than that stated in the service provision agreement, and they shall not be assigned to third parties, not even for maintenance thereof.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Upon compliance with the contractual covenant, processed personal data shall be destroyed, except when there is express authorization thereupon on behalf of the person to whom such services are delivered, if the possibility of future service requests is reasonably presumed, in which case they may be stored under proper safety conditions for a maximum two-year period.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. When delivering credit information service, only property-related personal data relevant to the individual's financial economic solvency and to the credit may be handled, provided that they have been obtained from sources available to the public, or from information furnished by the party involved or with the consent thereof.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Also personal data related to compliance or non-compliance with property obligations may be handled, if they have been furnished by the creditor or a person acting on his/her behalf.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. At the request of the data owner, the person in charge, or the user, of the database shall communicate to such holder any information, assessment and opinions thereupon furnished during the last six month-period, and the name and domicile of the relevant assignee in the event that data was obtained by way of assignment.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 4. Only personal data relevant to assess the economic and financial solvency of the parties involved during the last five years may be kept on file, recorded or assigned. Such term shall be reduced to two years if the debtor pays the debt or complies with the obligation, furnishing evidence of such payment or compliance.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 5. Delivery of credit information services shall not require the prior consent of, or notice upon, the data owner for assignment thereof, if such services are related to the assignees´ business or credit activities.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. In cases of domicile data gathering, documents distribution, advertising or direct selling and other similar business activities, data required to establish certain profiles for promotion, business or advertising purposes, or that may allow to establish consumer habits may be gathered; provided that such data be included in documents available to the public or be made available by data owners or obtained with their consent.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. In the events provided for in this Article, the data owner may exercise the right of access free of charge.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. At any time, the data owner may request deletion or blocking of its name from databases to which this Article refers.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Provisions hereof shall not apply to opinion polls, measurements and statistics made in accordance with Act Number 17622, market prospecting, scientific or medical research and similar activities, if data gathered can not be attributed to a specified person or to a person whose identity may be determined.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. If, during the data gathering process, it is not possible to maintain anonymity, the disaggregation technique shall be implemented, so that no person may be identified.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. The oversight authority shall take any steps necessary for compliance with purposes and other provisions hereof. To such effects, the oversight authority shall have the following duties and powers:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: closing paragraph
text: The Director shall be a full-time official, and job incompatibilities set forth herein for public officers shall apply thereto, and the Executive may remove him/her from office on the grounds of bad performance.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Associations or entities representing those in charge, or users, of privately-held databases may enact codes of professional conduct, which shall set forth rules for processing of personal data, tending to secure and improve information systems´ operating conditions in accordance with the principles set forth herein.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Such codes shall be registered in the appropriate registry under the responsibility of the oversight authority to such effect, and such competent authority may deny registry whenever it may consider that they do not comply with standing legal and regulatory provisions.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. Without prejudice to administrative liabilities applicable in the case of people in charge, or users, of public databases, the liability for damages derived from non-compliance with this Act, and applicable criminal sanctions, the competent authority may apply warning sanctions, suspension, and a one thousand pesos ($1,000) to one hundred thousand pesos ($100,000.) penalty, or instruct the closure or elimination of the file, record or database.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. Rules and regulations shall determine the conditions and proceedings for enforcement of the applicable sanctions, which shall be determined in relation to the seriousness and time of the violation involved, and of the damages derived from such violation, by ensuring the due process of law.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. The following Article shall be included as Article 117 bis of the Criminal Code:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. The following Article shall be included as Article 157 bis of the Criminal Code: “One-month to two-year imprisonment shall apply to any person who:

text: 1. The action for personal data protection or hábeas data shall apply:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: first paragraph
text: The action for personal data protection or habeas data may be exercised by the party involved, his/her guardians and successors or assigns of individuals, whether direct or indirect heirs up to the second degree of congeniality, per se or by an attorney.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: second paragraph
text: When the action is exercised by corporations, such action shall be inchoated by their legal representatives or attorneys appointed to such effect.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: third paragraph
text: The Ombudsman may intervene in the proceedings for legal assistance purposes.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: The action shall proceed against people in charge, and users, of public databases, and of private databases intended for reporting.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: first paragraph
text: The judge with jurisdiction in the domicile of the author, or the domicile of the defendant, or the place where the event or act took place or where the event or act could have effects, at the author’s election, shall have venue over these matters.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: second paragraph
text: Federal courts shall have venue over these matters:
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: The habeas data action shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions hereof and under the proceedings corresponding to the common summary proceeding to guarantee constitutional rights (acción de amparo) and, as a supplement, under the rules set forth in the Code of Civil and Commercial Proceedings, governing extraordinary summary proceeding (juicio sumarísimo).
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 1. The complaint shall be filed in writing, detailing as precisely as possible the file, record or database name and domicile and, if applicable, the name of the person in charge or user thereof.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: 1 second paragraph
text: In the case of public files, records or databases, the federal agency responsible for them shall be determined.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 2. The complainant may allege reasons for which he/she understands that the identified file, record or database includes information related to him/herself, the reasons why he/she considers that the information related to him/herself is discriminatory, false or inaccurate, and he/she may also furnish evidence of compliance with requirements applicable to exercise of rights granted thereto by this Act.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 3. The party involved may request that, while proceedings are pending, a notice be included in the record or database to the effects that the challenged information is subject to judicial proceedings.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 4. The Court may instruct the provisional file blocking as it refers to the personal datum from which the trial arose, provided that the discriminatory, false or inaccurate nature of the relevant information is patent.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: 5. In order to require information from the file, record or database involved, the Court shall apply a broad criterion to the relevant circumstances of subArticles 1 and 2.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: i
text: i. Upon admission of the action, the Court shall require from the file, record or database to send information related to the complainant. Likewise, the Court may request reports about data technical support, basic documents relating to data collection and any other aspect conducive to a case solution, as it may deem convenient.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: ii
text: ii. There shall be a maximum of five business days available to answer the report, which term may be prudently extended by the Court.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: i
text: i. Private records, files or databases shall not allege confidentiality of information required therefrom, save where journalistic information sources are affected.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: ii
text: ii. When a public file, record or database denies to send the requested report raising defenses of right of access, editing or deletion authorized by this Act or by a specific Act, such file, record or database shall furnish evidence of the facts that make such defense applicable. In such events, the Court may personally and directly get in contact with the requested data, thus assuring confidentiality thereupon.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: When answering the report, the file, record or database shall state the reasons why it included such challenged information and why it did not meet the request made by the interested party, in accordance with Articles 13 to 15 hereof.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: Upon answer to the report, the complainant may, within a three-day period amend the complaint requesting deletion, editing, confidentiality or updating of his/her personal data, if applicable hereunder, furnishing evidence thereof in the same act. Notice of this amended complaint shall be served upon the defendant within a three-day term.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: a
text: a) Upon maturity of the term to answer the report or upon filing of an answer thereto, and in the event provided for in Article 42, after answer to the amended complaint has been filed, and after the evidence been furnished thereon, the Court shall render judgment.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: b
text: b) In case the action is deemed to proceed, the Court shall specify whether the information shall be deleted, edited, updated or declared confidential, establishing a term for compliance thereof.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: c
text: c) If the action is rejected, the defendant shall not be presumed liable.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: d
text: d) In any event, judgment shall be notified to the oversight authority, which shall keep a record to such effect.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: first paragraph
text: The rules hereof contained in Chapters I, II, III, and IV, and in Article 32 are public and apply in the entire national territory.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: second paragraph
text: Provinces are invited to endorse to regulations of this Act that may exclusively apply to the federal jurisdiction.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: third paragraph
text: The federal jurisdiction shall govern with regard to records, files, or databases interconnected by interjurisdictional, national or international, networks.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: The Executive shall pass the regulations governing this Act and shall create a competent authority within a one hundred and eighty day term following enactment hereof.
deadline_or_term: one hundred and eighty day term
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

label: single paragraph
text: Files, records or databases intended to furnish information, existing at the time of the enactment of this Act, shall be registered in the registry created in accordance with Article 21, and shall be adapted to the provisions hereof within the term set forth by pertinent regulations.
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: Article 47. — (vetoed)
source_document: KB 2/South America/Argentina Personal Data Protection Act 2000.pdf

text: Be notified to the Executive.
